This week, we continued debate on fiscal year 2027 funding bills, including funding for the Government Accountability Office. This office has kept past administrations, both Democratic and Republican, in check and helped guide Congress to prevent fraud, waste, and abuse.

Unfortunately, House Republican leaders are pushing to gut the GAO by 25% at a time when the public – as well as Democrats and Republicans in Congress – have mounting concerns about the conduct of the Administration – from unauthorized wars abroad to self-administered slush funds.

Yesterday, the House Appropriations Committee debated the Fiscal Year 2027 Energy and Water Development and Related Agencies funding bill. While it did a good job supporting Army Corps of Engineers projects which help many communities with vital waterways and flood mitigation, its shortcomings outweigh its positive elements.

It cuts programs that help us diversify our energy supply chain and make sure that America stays on the cutting edge of research and development, it undermines nuclear security, and it abandons communities dealing with nuclear contamination from past defense projects. As a result, American families and businesses are going to face higher fuel and utility costs and many communities will be left less safe.

During the debate, I tried to improve the bill by supporting an amendment that would increase the critical minerals and energy innovation fund and restore the electricity account. This would help make America more energy independent, maintain the electrical grid and help make sure it is reliable, and ensure that we are not relying on foreign adversaries for materials vital to manufacturing and technology that drive our economy.

The amendment would help make sure that American families can afford to keep the lights on, farmers can operate, and local businesses can continue to function.

In July of 2024, while President Trump was campaigning in Butler, Pennsylvania, a gunman fired at the President. As the bullet grazed his ear on live television, I, as well as most Americans, were left in a state of disbelief and shock. This attempted assassination was chilling. It was a horrific attack of democracy and was just simply un-American.

This was an event I hoped our nation would never experience again. Yet, just two months later, authorities reported another attempted assassination of the President. In September of 2024, a man was spotted hiding in the bushes with a rifle aiming at the golf course where President Trump was golfing in Florida. Luckily, a Secret Service agent engaged the suspect before President Trump came into the shooter’s view. Nonetheless, it was another attempted attack on our President and, therefore, our nation.

Then, this weekend, a gunman with multiple weapons stormed the event venue of the White House Correspondents Dinner. Shots were fired, one of our brave Secret Service agents was hit, and the attacker left behind a manifesto claiming all Trump Administration officials, excluding one, were his targets. Luckily, no one was injured. However, the fact of the matter is this: this is the third time in less than two years that President Trump has faced an assassination attempt.

This should make every American, regardless of their political views, stop and reflect on the condition of our current culture and why this is happening.

Political violence is never acceptable – and I truly do believe the majority of Americans instinctively reject political violence. Most of us know what happened on Saturday night is wrong. Yet, as we reflect on this horrific event, we ought to think about what this political violence represents. To me, it symbolizes a deeper problem within our own society, culture, and political system.

Political rhetoric in our country has gotten out of hand. I am not naïve. I know that reckless rhetoric is not a tactic used by just one political party. However, today, I am speaking about the three assassination attempts on President Trump.

When I hear politicians compare the President to Hitler or compare federal law enforcement agencies like Immigration and Customs Enforcement and Border Patrol to Nazi Germany’s Gestapo and SS, I am appalled. Anyone who has read the history books knows how false and out of touch with reality those comparisons are. Moreover, it should be obvious that such rhetoric is dangerous. In fact, this kind of rhetoric is exactly what fuels the unstable and violence prone members of our society to act.

So, while I do think there will be almost a universal rejection by elected officials of the violence that occurred at the event on Saturday, I encourage all elected officials to think more deeply. I encourage them to stop and look at their own rhetoric when speaking about the President and their other political opponents. If that language is provocative, they ought to correct it immediately. Furthermore, I urge all American citizens to condemn politicians – from either party – who use problematic language when talking about the President, federal agencies, or other politicians. Dangerous rhetoric must end immediately.

The second thing we ought to remember is that many of the law enforcement officials who bravely and swiftly acted to protect the President, Vice President, our Cabinet members, and many of my colleagues on Saturday night are currently operating under an agency that is not funded. The events at the White House Correspondents Dinner this weekend demonstrate just how unacceptable it is to fail to fund the government, particularly the Department of Homeland Security, during this time of threats from abroad and political turmoil at home.

It is a huge mistake not to fund DHS and the selfless law enforcement agents who work within that agency. We should never, ever close an agency that protects not just the President, but every American citizen. It is unacceptable and reckless.

Finally, I want to make this clear: the House, under the leadership of Speaker Johnson, has voted to fully fund DHS five separate times. It is the Senate that has failed to do so – and not because the majority of the Senate doesn’t favor it. In fact, the majority of both chambers have voted to fund the Department of Homeland Security repeatedly. The hold up during this time of threats to our nation is all because of the misuse of a Senate rule, the filibuster. This is an issue I will delve into deeper during a later column.

So, what do we, as a nation, do now? In this moment, we should correct dangerous political rhetoric, move to immediately fund the agencies that keep us safe, and unite as a nation. We must not allow these types of horrific attacks to persist. As President Trump said in his statement after the assassination attempt in Butler, we must “show our True Character as Americans, remaining Strong and Determined.”

The United States of America is the greatest country this Earth has ever known. We must not allow evil from within to undermine our traditions of peaceful dissent and respect for those who hold opposing political views. Surely that is something that all Americans, regardless of party, can accept, celebrate, and practice when engaged in political debate and discussion.

I strongly oppose the Trump administration’s disruptive decision to require many students, temporary visa holders, and other individuals seeking green cards to leave the United States and return to their home countries while their applications are processed.

This policy creates unnecessary fear and uncertainty for families, workers, and employers who are following the law.

The Administration disregards the fact that many individuals seeking permanent residency are here legally and waiting for their cases to move through an already backlogged immigration system.

America has long benefited from attracting top researchers, doctors, engineers, entrepreneurs, and innovators through our legal immigration system and worker visa programs. Forcing these individuals to leave the United States during the green card process will deprive our country of their innovation, their tax contributions, and the many ways they strengthen our economy and communities.

As the son of Indian immigrants, I know firsthand that our nation is strengthened by people who come here legally, work hard, and contribute to our communities. We should be reducing processing delays and modernizing our immigration system, not creating additional barriers for people who are following the rules.

I support legal challenges to this policy and expect the courts to halt its implementation.

As the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda face another deadly and rapidly spreading Ebola outbreak, we are seeing in real time why global health security matters. Infectious diseases do not respect borders, and delays in disease detection and response make Americans more vulnerable.

Recognizing the persistent threat posed by Ebola and other infectious diseases, I introduced an amendment last year to the State Department reauthorization bill to strengthen Ebola response and global health security so the United States and our partners would be better prepared to stop outbreaks at their source before they reach our shores. 

Republicans voted it down.

Sweeping cuts to USAID and the CDC by this Administration have further weakened disease surveillance, reduced our ability to detect outbreaks early, and undermined the rapid response capacity that has helped protect Americans and save lives around the world.

We should be strengthening coordination with impacted countries, supporting frontline disease detection, and working alongside international organizations to contain outbreaks quickly and effectively.

RT by @RepMoolenaar: 🚨BREAKING | A new @ChinaSelect investigative report is out today and the findings are troubling. Our investigation and subsequent report found that @jpmorgan, @BankofAmerica, and @MorganStanley helped Chinese companies tied to the CCP’s military apparatus and forced Uyghur labor raise BILLIONS in global capital markets.

Just months after @DeptofWar designated Contemporary Amperex Technology Co., Ltd. (@catl_official), the world’s largest battery maker, as a “Chinese military company,” JPMorgan and Bank of America moved forward with underwriting its Hong Kong IPO, helping the company raise billions in new capital. According to our investigation, the banks proceeded even after CATL was linked to China’s Military-Civil Fusion strategy and despite evidence connecting the company to entities tied to the PLA, China’s defense-industrial base, and forced labor in Xinjiang.

The investigation uncovered CATL partnerships and business relationships with blacklisted Chinese defense-linked entities including @Huawei, NORINCO, CETC, @CSSC_global, COMAC, @ChinaMobile_X, and @CN_Nuclear_Corp. The report also details CATL’s ownership stake in Wuhu Shipyard, a key builder of Chinese naval vessels and military equipment, as well as research partnerships tied to the PLA’s National University of Defense Technology and China’s nuclear weapons complex.

The Committee found further evidence linking CATL’s supply chain to Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps (XPCC)-connected entities implicated in forced labor and the Uyghur genocide in Xinjiang. According to the investigation, CATL refused to provide full supply chain audits, while banks proceeded with the deals anyway despite public evidence and internal diligence reports identifying ongoing exposure to forced labor risks.

In a separate transaction, Morgan Stanley sponsored the IPO of Zijin Gold even after its parent company and Xinjiang subsidiaries were added to the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act Entity List. Internal documents showed the firm identified significant sanctions and national security risks and moved forward regardless.

Our investigation concluded that Wall Street’s due diligence processes prioritized deal completion over national security and human rights concerns. Policy changes are needed to stop U.S. financial institutions from bankrolling companies tied to the CCP’s military buildup and forced labor system.

More on the report here: https://chinaselectcommittee.house.gov/media/press-releases/jpmorgan-chase-and-bank-of-america-helped-a-chinese-military-company-raise-billions-of-dollars

F000466.text:
From Bristol to Washington Crossing to Hatfield, across our community this Memorial Day weekend, we have gathered in solemn gratitude to honor generations of brave Americans who gave their lives in the name of freedom.

Special thanks to Penndel American Legion Post #436, Fallsington American Legion Post 834, the Guardians of the Washington Crossing National Cemetery, Joseph A. Schumacher VFW Post 1597, and the many veterans, volunteers, and community organizations who continue to lead our community in this sacred duty of remembrance.

In every prayer offered, every flag raised, every wreath laid, and every family standing in remembrance, we are reminded of the enduring truth of this day: the blessings of liberty endure because generations of Americans were willing to defend them at the cost of their own lives.

Perhaps most moving has been the unity on display—veterans, Gold Star families, first responders, children, and neighbors standing shoulder to shoulder, bound together by gratitude, reverence, and the sacred duty to remember.

May we honor our fallen not only with our words today, but with how we live every day—as one, united community and grateful nation, worthy of their sacrifice.

May God bless our fallen heroes, may He comfort their Gold Star families, and may He continue to bless the United States of America.

Fair maps. Open participation. A government that answers to the people.

That should not be controversial—and every elected official, at every level of government, should be able to agree with it without hesitation.

Ahead of Memorial Day weekend, I was honored to join my friends from @WithHonorAction and colleagues from both parties, including several distinguished gentlemen and friends, the last three Vietnam veterans serving in Congress—Jim Baird, Mike Thompson, and Jack Bergman—for the annual washing of the Vietnam Veterans Memorial.

At that Wall, there are no Republicans or Democrats—only Americans, standing in gratitude before the more than 58,000 names of heroes who answered their nation’s call and never came home.

For too many Vietnam veterans and Gold Star families, the gratitude owed to them came far too late. Our duty now is to remember fully, to speak their names with reverence, and ensure their service and sacrifice—and of all who gave everything for our nation—are never forgotten.

As we enter Memorial Day weekend, may we pause and remember what this sacred holiday is truly about and honor our fallen not only with our words, but in how we live, serve, and stand together every day as one nation.

Thank you to Mesa County Commissioner Bobbie Daniel for traveling to Washington to testify before the House Natural Resources Subcommittee on Federal Lands in support of my Forest Health and Wildfire Risk Reduction Act.

This Memorial Day weekend, we honor Fr. Emil Kapaun of Pilsen, Kansas, who died on this day in 1951. A Catholic priest, Army chaplain, and American hero, Fr. Kapaun served with extraordinary courage alongside the 8th Cavalry Regiment, 1st Cavalry Division during the Korean War.

After being captured as a prisoner of war, he continued to minister to fellow prisoners, offering hope, prayer, and comfort while sacrificing the little food and strength he had for others. Even in the darkest conditions, his faith and selflessness never wavered. Fr. Kapaun was posthumously awarded the Medal of Honor in 2013.

His sacrifice, bravery, and devotion to God and country inspires us to this day.

Our office appreciated the opportunity to continue discussions with the White House as recovery efforts move forward across the CNMI following Super Typhoon Sinlaku. 

As our islands work through the challenges ahead, continued federal engagement and coordination remain critical to supporting recovery, rebuilding infrastructure, and ensuring communities have the resources needed to move forward.

Our office was proud to recognize on the House Floor the extraordinary response efforts following Super Typhoon Sinlaku and the many individuals, organizations, first responders, medical workers, volunteers, and community groups who stepped up for the Commonwealth during one of our most difficult moments. 

Their resilience, compassion, and commitment to helping others continue driving recovery efforts forward across the CNMI.

Our office is grateful to stand alongside the many volunteers, nonprofits, faith-based organizations, and community leaders who continue supporting families across the CNMI following Super Typhoon Sinlaku. 

Recovery is only possible because so many people have stepped forward to help their neighbors, distribute critical supplies, and bring communities together during this difficult time.

The compassion, coordination, and dedication shown across our islands continue making a meaningful difference for countless families as recovery efforts move forward.

For the CNMI, transportation infrastructure is not about convenience, it is about survival. 

When roads, ports, and airports fail in island communities thousands of miles from the mainland, the impacts are immediate and far reaching, affecting emergency response, supply chains, economic activity, and the daily lives of our people.

I testified in support of H.R. 8870, the BUILD America 250 Act, because strengthening investment in territorial transportation systems means strengthening public safety, disaster resilience, commerce, tourism, and long term economic sustainability in the Northern Mariana Islands. 

The territories are on the front lines of America’s strategic interests in the Pacific, and our infrastructure must reflect that reality.

Our office is proud to share that the Commonwealth’s Criminal Justice Planning Agency has been awarded $500,000 through the Department of Justice’s Office on Violence Against Women to strengthen the CNMI’s response to domestic violence, dating violence, sexual assault, and stalking cases. 

This funding will support specialized law enforcement training, enhanced investigative efforts, victim services, policy and procedure reviews, and the development of protocols for processing untested sexual assault kits to help improve protections and support for victims across the Commonwealth.

M001239.text: It was an honor to speak at the Virginia Veterans Cemetery Memorial Day ceremony in Amelia this morning. We will never forget the brave men and women who paid the ultimate sacrifice for our freedom, and the loved ones they leave behind.
In observance of Memorial Day, my offices will be closed, Monday, May, 25th.

Memorial Day is more than a long weekend it is a sacred reminder that liberty has a cost. Generations of brave warriors answered the call to serve, knowing they might never come home. They fought for our flag, our families, and the American way of life, and they paid the ultimate sacrifice.

Today, we honor their courage and mourn their loss. And we thank God for the warriors who stood in defense of freedom against every enemy.
May we live worthy of their sacrifice, remain steadfast in our love for this country, and never forget those who gave everything so America could endure.

God bless our fallen heroes, and God bless the United States of America.
